newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico agriculture minister raps U.S. tomato pact.
newsitem.headline: Mexico agriculture minister raps U.S. tomato pact.

text.p: Mexican Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa on Wednesday criticised the tomato dumping resolution reached earlier this week by the U.S. Commerce Department.

"What they are doing is putting a minimum barrier on prices, which will do more damage to producers," Labastida said, referring to the 21 cent per pound base price for imported winter tomatoes to the United States.
The U.S. government decision is related to the "tomato war", which began when Florida farmers complained Mexicans were dumping tomatoes in the U.S. market.

Labastida said the decision would probably shrink Mexican exports to the United States and could cost some workers their jobs. There are about 300,000 tomato farm workers in the states of Sinaloa, Oaxaca, Zacatecas and Guerrero.
